newsitem.title: FINLAND: Helsinki starts touch lower, eyes on U.S. payrolls.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki starts touch lower, eyes on U.S. payrolls.

text.p: * Shares open slightly lower in very quiet trade as Wall Street falls on jitters ahead of U.S. July payrolls data due at 1530/1230 GMT. Nokia touch down matching its overnight New York close. Some profit-taking seen ahead of its Q2 results Monday.
* Volume 22 million markka, 47.9 pct in Nokia

Shares started slightly in thre red on Friday as Nokia opened a touch off to match its lower close on Wall Street, where the Dow eased on jitters ahead of U.S. July payrolls data due at 1530/1230 GMT, brokers said.
Some brokers said profit-taking could emerge in Nokia ahead of the release of its Q2 results on Monday.

"The result is expected to be good, but the share has risen so much after Ericsson's results (last week) that some profit-taking could emerge today, or at the latest on Monday," one broker said, adding, she expected profit-taking only in a narrow five markka range.

Trade was very quiet at open with the market subdued ahead of the release of U.S. July payrolls and unemployment data at 1530/1230 GMT. Economists polled by Reuters expect non-farm payrolls to have risen by 193,000. A stronger than expected figure may undermine the recent broad rally.
Raisio was largely unchanged around 603.00 markka after Thursday's volatility on news that a U.S. company may launch a product competing with Raisio's Benecol.
Outokumpu rose 2.00 markka to 106.00, boosted by rising zinc prices and the strong dollar, brokers said.
